hints.title: Consider Base Case
hints.text: When there is only one passenger, they will always take their assigned first seat with probability 1.0.

hints.title: Symmetry Between First and Last Seats
hints.text: The first person either picks their own seat (safe) or the nth seat (doomed), with equal probability whenever choices arise.

hints.title: Constant Probability for n Greater Than One
hints.text: For any number of passengers greater than one, symmetry ensures the nth person gets their seat with probability exactly 0.5.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating random seat assignments across n passengers requires Monte Carlo approximation or factorial states.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Mathematical symmetry solves the question in constant time and zero memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain why the probability is independent of n for n >= 2 using symmetry.
complexity.notes: Returns 1.0 when n equals 1, and 0.5 for all n >= 2.
